results.title: The Auditable Assembly Line: A Deep Dive into Data CI/CD for Scalable MLOps | by Dálio Lage | Medium
results.content: This contract ensures that only validated, versioned, and tested data proceeds to the next stage. ## Why Data CI/CD is the Missing Link in MLOps. MLOps, in borrowing its principles from DevOps, naturally focused on what it knew best: versioning, testing, and deploying code. 1. **Consistency and Reproducibility:** Every model training run, whether on a data scientist’s notebook or a production cluster, uses a validated and versioned snapshot of data. Building an effective Data CI/CD pipeline requires orchestrating specialized tools in a logical seven-stage sequence. Versioning**Create an immutable, atomic snapshot of the validated data with lineage.lakeFS, DVC, Delta Lake Time Travel**Consider:** Scalability to large datasets (billions of objects). **Anti-Pattern:** Testing only model code; data transformations and feature logic are equally bug-prone.**5. Build & Push**Package all artifacts (code, validated data pointers, model) into a reproducible container/wheel.Docker, Poetry**Consider:** Multi-stage Docker builds to keep production images lean. **Verdict for MLOps:** Use **Great Expectations** at the validation gate (Stage 2) to enforce a static contract on incoming data (schema, types, nulls). **Data Engineering & Platform Teams.** Building robust production data lakes and enabling CI/CD for data pipelines. **Verdict for MLOps:** For building a scalable, enterprise-grade Data CI/CD pipeline, **lakeFS** is the architecturally superior choice. Instead, the image should contain code that fetches the versioned data and model at runtime, using a pointer (e.g., a lakeFS commit hash) passed as an environment variable. In a pull request workflow, when a data scientist adds a new feature, the PR should include not only the feature engineering code but also a new `pytest` test function in `tests/test_data_quality.py` that validates this new feature (e.g., `test_new_feature_is_within_expected_range`). The CI pipeline runs these tests, blocking the merge if the data quality logic is flawed, ensuring data quality evolves alongside features. Integrating a feature store elevates the Data CI/CD pipeline. The system detects a problem, fetches the latest version of validated data, retrains, validates, and deploys the new model, all without human intervention. The Data CI/CD architecture, therefore, doesn’t just make ML models more reliable; it builds high-assurance data systems that can withstand scrutiny in any domain where data integrity is paramount, including finance, healthcare, and government.

results.title: Host Your Bitnami Docker Images Locally: Avoid Breakage When Providers Change the Rules | by Vincenthartmann | Medium
results.content: # Host Your Bitnami Docker Images Locally: Avoid Breakage When Providers Change the Rules. In recent years, several vendors (Red Hat, Docker, Bitnami…) have tightened access to their images and shifted their offerings toward paid plans or Legacy repositories. The result: versioned tags vanish, public images stop receiving updates, and CI/CD pipelines can break if you aren’t prepared. * the need to either pay for a managed secured image offering or take responsibility for building and hosting your own images. ## Proposed solution: build + host a `kubectl` image internally. 3. builds the image, tags it with `latest` and the version, tests it, and pushes it to your private registry. #!/bin/bashset -e # Exit on error# Configuration variablesDOCKER_REGISTRY=""DOCKER_NAMESPACE="docker_mirror"IMAGE_NAME="kubectl"IMAGE_TAG="latest"DOCKERFILE_PATH="./Dockerfile"echo "🚀 Starting kubectl image build and push process..."# 1. Create Dockerfile dynamicallyecho "📄 Creating Dockerfile..."cat > $DOCKERFILE_PATH << EOFFROM alpine:latest# Install base dependenciesRUN apk add --no-cache \\ curl \\ bash \\ ca-certificates \\ && update-ca-certificates# Copy kubectlCOPY kubectl /usr/local/bin/kubectlRUN chmod +x /usr/local/bin/kubectl# Verify installationRUN kubectl version --client# Non-root user for securityRUN addgroup -g 1001 kubectl && \\ adduser -D -s /bin/bash -u 1001 -G kubectl kubectlUSER kubectlWORKDIR /home/kubectlCMD ["/bin/bash"]EOF# 4. Build Docker imageecho "🐳 Building Docker image..."FULL_IMAGE_NAME="${DOCKER_REGISTRY}/${DOCKER_NAMESPACE}/${IMAGE_NAME}:${IMAGE_TAG}"VERSIONED_IMAGE_NAME="${DOCKER_REGISTRY}/${DOCKER_NAMESPACE}/${IMAGE_NAME}:${KUBECTL_VERSION#v}"docker build -t $FULL_IMAGE_NAME -t $VERSIONED_IMAGE_NAME .# 5. Test the image (optional)echo "🧪 Testing the image..."docker run --rm $FULL_IMAGE_NAME kubectl version --client# 6. Push the imageecho "📤 Pushing the image to the registry..."docker push $FULL_IMAGE_NAMEdocker push $VERSIONED_IMAGE_NAME# 8. Cleanupecho "🧹 Cleaning up temporary files..."rm -f kubectl $DOCKERFILE_PATHecho "✅ Process completed successfully!"echo "📋 Images available:"echo " - $FULL_IMAGE_NAME"echo " - $VERSIONED_IMAGE_NAME"# 9. Commands to use the imageecho ""echo "🔧 To use the image:"echo " docker run -it --rm $FULL_IMAGE_NAME"echo " docker run -it --rm -v ~/.kube:/home/kubectl/.kube $FULL_IMAGE_NAME". For organizations lacking mature DevOps capabilities, paying for a managed offering (e.g., Bitnami Secure Images or similar commercial services) may still be the simplest path. The migration of public images to Legacy repositories is a reminder that relying on third-party registries creates technical debt and operational risk. Building and hosting your critical images (here demonstrated with `kubectl`) is a pragmatic step to regain control over your deployment pipeline and increase pipeline resilience.

results.title: Handling Backward Compatibility in Versioned Product APIs | Agile Seekers
results.content: ## Handling Backward Compatibility in Versioned Product APIs. When a digital product relies on APIs to deliver functionality to external developers, partner integrations, or internal systems, maintaining backward compatibility becomes critical. That’s why a well-planned approach to backward compatibility in versioned APIs is a cornerstone of scalable product management. This post explores the practical strategies for managing backward compatibility in versioned product APIs. It includes key design principles, implementation techniques, and governance practices that support long-term API health without sacrificing innovation. Backward compatibility ensures that existing API clients continue to function correctly even as the API evolves. For professionals in Project Management Professional certification and those involved in SAFe Product Owner/Manager certification, managing API versions without breaking clients is an essential skill. ## Versioning as a Tool for Compatibility. Major version changes (v2.0.0) may introduce breaking changes, while minor/patch updates remain backward compatible. ## When to Deprecate an API Version. Handling backward compatibility in versioned APIs requires foresight, planning, and communication.

results.title: Jenkins CI/CD Pipeline for Building and Pushing Docker Images of a Simple Hello World API Implemented in FastAPI to Docker Hub | by Chnarsimha | Medium
results.content: # Jenkins CI/CD Pipeline for Building and Pushing Docker Images of a Simple Hello World API Implemented in FastAPI to Docker Hub. In this tutorial, we will guide you through the process of setting up a Jenkins CI/CD pipeline to automate the building and pushing of Docker images to Docker Hub. We will use a simple FastAPI “Hello World” application as our example code. * Streamline your development workflow with Jenkins by creating a CI/CD pipeline that automates the build and push of Docker images. * Elevate your containerized applications with a robust CI/CD pipeline, empowering you to focus on code changes while Jenkins handles the Docker image lifecycle. * **Internet Access from Jenkins Server**:Ensure that the Jenkins server has internet access to pull Docker images and push to Docker Hub.
